claims.text: Data-driven machine learning can optimize multi-step thermo-mechanical processing in conventional metallic alloys.
Machine-learning-optimized thermo-mechanical processing can produce tailored microstructures.
The tailored microstructures can simultaneously improve strength and ductility.
The initial materials are conventional metallic alloys with standard grain structures.
A machine-learning model is used to determine optimal thermo-mechanical processing parameters.
The proposed improvement applies under ambient conditions and standard mechanical loading.
The optimized processing produces engineered microstructures containing tailored coherent precipitates.
The optimized processing produces dual-phase lamellar structures.
Precise tuning of strengthening-phase formation and distribution decouples the conventional strength–ductility trade-off.
Tuning the strengthening phases enhances strength without compromising ductility.
Machine-learning-optimized processing will increase both strength and ductility relative to conventional trial-and-error processing.
The approach may be limited to alloys whose microstructural evolution is highly sensitive to processing parameters.
The approach may require sufficient experimental data to train the machine-learning model.
Incomplete mapping of processing–microstructure–property relationships may reduce the predictive accuracy of the machine-learning model.
